title: What Counts as Chemistry Evidence?
purpose: Establish scientific inquiry, chemical evidence, and reliable sources.
labDataRequirement: Use a paper-based evidence investigation. No chemicals are handled. Students compare claim cards, observation notes, and data snippets.
safetyNotes: This lesson uses written scenarios only. Do not taste, smell, mix, or handle unknown substances to create evidence.
simulationReview: Direct simulation/resource link is provided in P01.html and in directSimulationUrl.
assessmentStimulusNeeded: Use the Unit 1 matrix requirement for this lesson: embedded scenario, table, graph, model, diagram, or organizer as needed.
simulationVirtualLabReviewRequirement: Required for safety/procedure practice, measurement/data analysis, and particle models
simulationVirtualLabReviewFocus: Evidence/source classification using chemical claims, observations, and data
directSimulationStudentTask: After the simulation opens, use the Sandwich Shop screen as the evidence model for claims and data. Change the starting amounts of the ingredients one at a time. Observe what product is made and which ingredient is left over. Record the starting amounts, product amount, leftover amount, and one claim that is supported by the data.
simulationReviewImplementation: Student-facing lesson includes one exact direct simulation/resource link plus adjacent step-by-step directions for what to open, click/use, observe, record, and connect to the lesson standard.
simulationSourceReference: CPALMS resources; OpenStax Chemistry 2e scientific method sections; ACS education resources
